title: Origin and Evolution of Life
subject: Biology
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET / NEET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Theories of Origin of Life & Chemical Evolution
points: Historical theories: Special Creation (Father Suarez), Panspermia (spores from space), Spontaneous Generation / Abiogenesis (life from decaying matter; disproved by Louis Pasteur's swan-necked flask experiment: 'Omne vivum ex vivo').
Chemical Evolution (Oparin-Haldane Theory, 1924-1929): Life originated from non-living organic molecules through biochemical evolution in primitive oceans ('hot dilute prebiotic soup').

Primitive earth environment: Highly reducing atmosphere containing methane (CH₄), ammonia (NH₃), hydrogen (H₂), and water vapor (H₂O); completely lacked free molecular oxygen (O₂). High temperature, UV rays, and lightning supplied energy.

Protobionts: Non-living macromolecular aggregates showing metabolic-like properties: Coacervates (Oparin: colloid droplets without lipid bilayer) and Microspheres (Sydney Fox: proteinoid droplets with selective boundary).

formulas.label: Primitive earth conditions vs Modern earth
formulas.expr: Primitive: Reducing atmosphere (CH₄, NH₃, H₂, H₂O vapor; NO free O₂) | Modern: Oxidizing atmosphere (21% O₂)

formulas.label: Chemical evolution sequence
formulas.expr: Inorganic atoms → Simple molecules (H₂O, NH₃, CH₄) → Simple organic (amino acids, sugars) → Macromolecules → Protobionts → First cells

nodes.title: Urey and Miller's Simulation Experiment (1953)
points: Experimental setup: Spark discharge glass apparatus simulating prebiotic earth conditions.
Gas mixture: Methane (CH₄), Ammonia (NH₃), and Hydrogen (H₂) in ratio 2 : 1 : 2, along with continuous steam from boiling water.
Energy source: High-voltage electric discharge (~75,000 volts via tungsten electrodes, ~800 °C) simulating lightning.

Results & Analysis: After running continuously for 1 week, condensed fluid turned red-brown. Chemical analysis revealed synthesis of simple amino acids: Glycine, Alanine, and Aspartic acid, along with organic acids and nitrogen bases, confirming Oparin-Haldane chemical evolution.

formulas.label: Miller-Urey gas ratio formula
formulas.expr: CH₄ : NH₃ : H₂ = 2 : 1 : 2 (with boiling H₂O steam, 800 °C, electric spark)

formulas.label: Synthesized amino acids in Miller's experiment
formulas.expr: Glycine (simplest), Alanine, Aspartic acid

nodes.title: Morphological & Anatomical Evidences of Evolution
points: 1. Homologous Organs (Divergent Evolution): Organs with similar structural design and embryonic origin, but adapted to perform different functions (e.g. Forelimbs of Human, Cheetah, Whale, and Bat; Bougainvillea thorns and Cucurbita tendrils). Indicates common ancestry.

2. Analogous Organs (Convergent Evolution): Organs with different anatomical structures and embryonic origins, but performing similar functions under similar selective pressures (e.g. Wings of butterfly and wings of birds; Eye of Octopus and eye of Mammals; Flippers of Penguins and Dolphins; Sweet potato root tuber and Potato stem tuber).

3. Vestigial Organs: Non-functional, reduced remnants of structures that were functional in ancestral species (e.g. Vermiform appendix, Nictitating membrane / plica semilunaris, Wisdom teeth, Coccyx / tailbone).
4. Atavism (Reversion): Reappearance of ancestral characteristics (e.g. human baby born with tail, extra nipples, thick body hair).

formulas.label: Homology vs Analogy comparison key
formulas.expr: Homology: Same origin, different function → Divergent evolution (Common ancestor) | Analogy: Different origin, same function → Convergent evolution

formulas.label: Vestigial organs in human body
formulas.expr: Vermiform appendix, Wisdom teeth (3rd molars), Plica semilunaris, Ear pinna muscles, Coccyx

nodes.title: Paleontological & Embryological Evidences
points: Paleontology: Study of fossils (remnants or impressions of past organisms preserved in sedimentary rocks).

Archaeopteryx lithographica: Classic connecting link between Reptiles and Birds. Reptilian features: Teeth in jaws, long bony tail with free caudal vertebrae, claws on digits, solid non-pneumatic bones; Avian features: Feathers, wings, beak, four-toed perching foot.
Living fossils: Surviving species showing minimal change over millions of years (Latimeria / Coelacanth lobe-finned fish, Limulus king crab, Sphenodon, Ginkgo biloba).

Embryological Evidences: Ernst Haeckel's Biogenetic Law ('Ontogeny recapitulates Phylogeny' - embryonic development mirrors evolutionary ancestry). Disproved by Karl Ernst von Baer, who showed embryos never pass through adult stages of other animals.

formulas.label: Connecting link: Archaeopteryx traits
formulas.expr: Reptilian (teeth, long bony tail, claws) + Avian (feathers, wings, beak)

formulas.label: Biogenetic law statement
formulas.expr: Ontogeny (individual embryonic development) recapitulates Phylogeny (evolutionary ancestry)

nodes.title: Theories of Evolution: Lamarckism vs Darwinism
points: 1. Lamarckism (Jean-Baptiste de Lamarck, 1809): Theory of inheritance of acquired characters and use/disuse of organs (e.g. Giraffe's long neck). Disproved by August Weismann's Germplasm Theory (cut tails of mice for 22 generations; somatic changes are not transmitted to gametes).
2. Darwinism (Charles Darwin, 1859 - 'Origin of Species by Natural Selection'): Inspired by HMS Beagle voyage to Galapagos and Malthus' Essay on Population.

Darwinian postulates: 1) Overproduction; 2) Limited food and space; 3) Struggle for existence (intraspecific, interspecific, environmental); 4) Variations; 5) Survival of the fittest (natural selection); 6) Speciation.
Drawbacks of Darwinism: Failed to explain source/origin of variations ('arrival of the fittest'); could not distinguish between heritable germinal variations and non-heritable somatic variations.

formulas.label: Darwinian natural selection sequence
formulas.expr: Overproduction → Struggle for existence → Variations → Survival of fittest → Natural Selection → Speciation

formulas.label: Germplasm theory (August Weismann)
formulas.expr: Somatoplasm (body cells, not inherited) vs Germplasm (gametes, inherited)

nodes.title: Mutation Theory & Modern Synthetic Theory of Evolution
points: 1. Mutation Theory (Hugo de Vries, 1901): Based on Evening Primrose (Oenothera lamarckiana). Proposed that evolution occurs via sudden, discontinuous, large, directionless mutations called Saltation (single step large mutation), unlike Darwin's slow, continuous, directional variations.
2. Modern Synthetic Theory of Evolution (Neo-Darwinism): Integration of Mendelian genetics, population genetics, and natural selection (Dobzhansky, Mayr, Stebbins).

5 Pillars of Modern Synthetic Theory: 1) Gene mutations (point mutations, frameshifts); 2) Gene recombination (crossing over during pachytene of meiosis I); 3) Chromosomal aberrations (deletion, duplication, inversion, translocation); 4) Natural selection (differential reproduction); 5) Reproductive isolation (geographical or genetic barriers preventing interbreeding).

formulas.label: Darwinian variation vs De Vries mutation
formulas.expr: Darwin: Small, gradual, directional | De Vries: Large, sudden, directionless (Saltation)

formulas.label: Modern Synthetic Theory equation of factors
formulas.expr: Evolution = Genetic Variations (Mutations + Recombination) + Natural Selection + Reproductive Isolation

nodes.title: Hardy-Weinberg Principle & Modes of Natural Selection
points: Hardy-Weinberg Principle (1908): In a large, randomly mating, diploid population, allele frequencies and genotype frequencies remain constant across generations in the absence of evolutionary forces.
Equations: Allele frequencies: p + q = 1; Genotype frequencies: p² + 2pq + q² = 1 (where p = freq of dominant allele A, q = freq of recessive allele a, p² = AA, 2pq = Aa, q² = aa).
Disrupting factors: Gene flow, Genetic drift (Sewall Wright effect in small populations, Founder effect, Bottleneck effect), Mutation, Recombination, Natural selection.

Modes of Natural Selection: 1) Stabilizing selection: Favors mean intermediate phenotypes, narrows peak (human birth weight ~3 kg); 2) Directional selection: Favors one extreme phenotype, shifts peak in one direction (Industrial melanism in Peppered moth Biston betularia, antibiotic resistance); 3) Disruptive selection: Favors both extreme phenotypes, forms two peaks.

formulas.label: Hardy-Weinberg allele frequency equation
formulas.expr: p + q = 1 (p = freq of A, q = freq of a)

formulas.label: Hardy-Weinberg genotype frequency equation
formulas.expr: p² + 2pq + q² = 1 (p² = AA, 2pq = Aa, q² = aa)

formulas.label: Three modes of Natural Selection
formulas.expr: Stabilizing (narrow peak, mean favored) | Directional (peak shifts to one side) | Disruptive (two peaks formed, extremes favored)

nodes.title: Adaptive Radiation & Speciation
points: Adaptive Radiation: Evolutionary diversification of a single ancestral species into multiple distinct ecological niches within a geographical area.

Examples: 1) Darwin's Finches on Galapagos Islands (seed-eating ancestral beak radiated into insectivorous, vegetarian, cactus-feeding, and warbler beaks); 2) Australian Marsupials (ancestral marsupial radiated into Tasmanian wolf, Wombat, Bandicoot, Kangaroo).

Convergent evolution of Placental Mammals & Marsupials: Distinct lineages evolving analogous adaptations: Placental wolf ↔ Tasmanian wolf; Mole ↔ Marsupial mole; Anteater ↔ Numbat; Flying squirrel ↔ Flying phalanger.

Speciation: Allopatric speciation (geographic isolation like mountains/rivers splits population); Sympatric speciation (reproductive isolation within same geographic range, e.g. polyploidy in plants).

formulas.label: Adaptive radiation definition
formulas.expr: Evolution of diverse species from a common ancestor radiating into different ecological niches

formulas.label: Convergent marsupial-placental analogues
formulas.expr: Tasmanian wolf ↔ Wolf | Anteater ↔ Numbat | Flying squirrel ↔ Flying phalanger

nodes.title: Human Evolution & Cranial Capacity Timeline
points: Human ancestral lineage chronologically:
1. Dryopithecus & Ramapithecus (15 mya): Dryopithecus was ape-like; Ramapithecus was more human-like and walked erect.
2. Australopithecus (2-3 mya, East Africa): Taung baby, Lucy; brain capacity 450-600 cc; bipedal, used stone tools, largely vegetarian.
3. Homo habilis ('Handy man', 1.7-2.0 mya): Cranial capacity 650-800 cc; first hominid tool-maker; did not eat meat.
4. Homo erectus (1.5 mya, Java/Peking man): Cranial capacity ~900 cc; upright bipedal posture; used fire and stone axes; ate meat.
5. Homo neanderthalensis (100,000-40,000 ya): Cranial capacity 1400 cc; lived in caves; used animal hides for clothing; buried dead with ceremonies.
6. Cro-Magnon man (Homo sapiens fossilis, 34,000 ya): Cranial capacity 1600 cc (largest cranial volume!); cave paintings.
7. Homo sapiens sapiens (Modern man, 25,000-10,000 ya): Cranial capacity 1350-1450 cc; agriculture arose ~10,000 years ago.

formulas.label: Cranial capacity chronological table
formulas.expr: H. habilis: 650-800 cc | H. erectus: 900 cc | H. neanderthalensis: 1400 cc | Cro-Magnon: 1600 cc | Modern man: 1350-1450 cc

formulas.label: Human evolution chronological pathway
formulas.expr: Dryopithecus → Ramapithecus → Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo neanderthalensis → Homo sapiens

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Hardy-Weinberg problem shortcut: If given recessive phenotype (aa) = 16% (0.16) → q² = 0.16 ⇒ q = 0.4 → p = 1 − 0.4 = 0.6 → Heterozygotes (2pq) = 2(0.6)(0.4) = 0.48 (48%)!
TRAP 2: Miller-Urey ratio: CH₄ : NH₃ : H₂ = 2 : 1 : 2. (Ammonia is 1; Methane and Hydrogen are 2).
TRAP 3: First hominid with human-like features = Homo habilis (first tool maker, 650-800 cc).
TRAP 4: Largest cranial capacity in human lineage = Cro-Magnon man (~1600 cc), higher than modern humans (1350-1450 cc)!

TRAP 5: Industrial melanism: Peppered moth (Biston betularia typica light vs carbonaria dark). Before industrialization: light moths favored by lichens. Post-industrialization: dark moths favored by soot-covered trunks (Directional selection!).

formulas.label: Hardy-Weinberg quick step-by-step hack
formulas.expr: Given recessive % = q² → take √ to get q → p = 1 − q → Carrier 2pq = 2 × p × q

formulas.label: Miller-Urey gas ratio mnemonic
formulas.expr: Methane (2) : Ammonia (1) : Hydrogen (2) [2:1:2]

formulas.label: Human cranial capacity ranking
formulas.expr: Cro-Magnon (1600 cc) > Neanderthal (1400 cc) > Modern Man (1350-1450 cc) > H. erectus (900 cc) > H. habilis (650-800 cc)
